description:
Pipelines whose reader exits early. A short writer finishes before the reader exits, as bash's
usually does into a pipe with room for its output, so `set -o pipefail` sees no SIGPIPE; a writer
that fills the pipe gets SIGPIPE, as in bash.

Each case name starts with `pipe readers: `.

cases.name: pipe readers: pipefail and errexit with head after a short loop
cases.script: set -euo pipefail; for i in 1 2 3; do echo $i; done | head -n 1; echo reached
cases.oracleRace: a writer still writing when `head` exits gets SIGPIPE (141) in bash

cases.name: pipe readers: short writers are not cut off
cases.script:
set -o pipefail
for i in 1 2 3; do echo $i; done | head -n 1; echo "loop $? ${PIPESTATUS[*]}"
printf '%s\n' a b c | head -1; echo "printf $?"
seq 3 | head -1; echo "seq $?"
{ echo a; echo b; echo c; } | head -n 1; echo "group $?"
f() { echo a; echo b; }; f | head -1; echo "function $?"
x=$(for i in 1 2 3; do echo $i; done | head -1); echo "substitution $? $x"
cases.oracleRace: a writer still writing when `head` exits gets SIGPIPE (141) in bash

cases.name: pipe readers: writers that fill the pipe get SIGPIPE
cases.script:
set -o pipefail
seq 100000 | head -1; echo "seq $?"
yes | head -1; echo "yes $?"
for i in $(seq 20000); do echo $i; done | head -1; echo "loop $? ${PIPESTATUS[*]}"
while :; do echo y; done | head -2; echo "while $?"
set -e; seq 100000 | head -1; echo not-reached

cases.name: pipe readers: a short writer is not cut off after other commands
cases.script:
set -o pipefail
r=; for k in $(seq 70); do for i in 1 2 3; do echo $i; done | head -n 1 >/dev/null; r=$r$?; :; done; echo "$r"
cases.oracleRace: a writer still writing when `head` exits gets SIGPIPE (141) in bash
